book.title: Mahagatha: 100 Tales from the Puranas
book.author: Satyarth Nayak
recognition: Dainik Jagran Kirti Samman (Hindi bestseller translation), per Google Books
Over 1,00,000 copies sold and 'Number 1 Bestseller', per publisher blurb
book.structure: 100 tales in one flat run, told in chronological order from creation in Satya Yuga to the start of Kali Yuga. No printed part headings were found. The yuga per tale below is inferred, not printed.
book.front_back_matter: Author's note (states the book's thesis that every event has a cause). The publisher page links a 'Notes & Bibliography' section; its contents were not seen.

rights.status: Copyrighted (2022). Use as a finding aid only.
rights.allowed: Use tale titles, our own one-line summaries and the book's ordering to choose subjects and find primary sources.
rights.not_allowed: Quoting, paraphrasing at length or adapting Nayak's prose; using or tracing Onkar Fondekar's illustrations; copying the book's chapter sequence as a film's structure.
rights.narration_rule: Any film built on a tale is researched from the Puranas themselves (public-domain translations where possible) through technical-researcher, never from this book's text.

use_with.brief_categories: mythology (being added to specs/categories.json by a parallel session, uncommitted on 2026-11-23); fall back to storytelling if it is not merged. Add history when a film explains a place, festival or text.
use_with.styles: mythic-paper, carved-relief, painted-folio, shadow-lantern (experimental, catalogue/data/styles/); a mythic-tale template and skill were in progress but not on disk when this record was made.

provenance.titles: Tales 1-23 checked against the Google Books contents listing (id j8mSEAAAQBAJ). Tales 24-100 come from one source: Bookey's 'Summary Content List' (cdn.bookey.app/files/pdf/book/en/mahagatha.pdf), a third-party summary service whose list matches the 23 cross-checked titles exactly. Bookey drops the apostrophe in tale 100; the title is given here as Amazon prints it.
provenance.summaries: Written by us, in our own words, from Bookey's chapter notes and the traditional versions of each myth. Where the book's version could not be seen to its end, the summary says so.
provenance.puranic_sources: Our attribution of where each myth is commonly found, NOT the book's own citations (its notes were not seen). Confidence: high = well-known locus; medium = attested but the book's variant may differ; low = attribution not checked. Verify before any narration.
provenance.yuga: Inferred: tale 1 opens in Satya Yuga (per the blurb); Vamana (50) is traditionally the first avatar of Treta Yuga; Krishna's birth (84) opens Dwapara Yuga; Parikshit (100) is the first king of Kali Yuga. The 49/50 and 83/84 boundaries are our assumption.

vocabularies.form_fit: short = one twist or one 'why' answer that fits 20-60 s; mid = needs set-up and a payoff, 60-180 s. Arcs are candidates for a series or a long-form film.
vocabularies.care: Content needing editorial care on social platforms or for respectful handling.

tales.title: Brahma Begins Creation
tales.summary: From the formless Parabrahman come Om, the three gunas and the elements. Narayana lays the golden cosmic egg, and Brahma is born on a lotus from Vishnu's navel to begin creation.
tales.explains: The cosmic egg (Brahmanda); the three gunas

tales.title: Vishnu Kills Madhu and Kaitabha
tales.summary: Two demons born from Vishnu's earwax steal the Vedas and threaten Brahma. The goddess Nidra wakes Vishnu, who cannot beat them by force and tricks them into choosing their own death.

tales.title: Shiva Emerges
tales.summary: The Earth is shaped from the dead demons and the four yugas are set. Brahma's mind-born Kumaras refuse to have children, and from his frustration Rudra, Shiva, appears from his forehead.

tales.title: Brahma and Narada Fight
tales.summary: Brahma creates the Saptarishi and Dharma as a bull that will lose one leg per yuga. His son Narada refuses to help with creation, and father and son curse each other.
tales.explains: Dharma as a bull losing a leg each yuga

tales.title: Man Is Created
tales.summary: Shiva and Vishnu clash at Daksha's rite and are reconciled as Harihara. Shiva shows the stalled Brahma that creation needs Shakti by appearing as Ardhanarishvara, half man and half woman, which opens the way to the first humans.
tales.explains: Harihara; Ardhanarishvara; the first human pair

tales.title: Shiva Beheads Brahma
tales.summary: Under Narada's curse Brahma desires his own daughter, who flees through a hundred animal forms (hence Shatarupa) while he follows in matching forms. Shiva cuts off one of Brahma's heads and must carry the skull as penance.
tales.explains: Why Brahma has four heads; Shiva as skull-bearer

tales.title: Narada and Maya
tales.summary: Narada asks Vishnu what maya is, is distracted by a young woman, marries, raises a family and loses them all in a flood, then wakes beside Vishnu to find the whole life was illusion.

tales.title: Jaya and Vijaya
tales.summary: Vaikuntha's gatekeepers turn away the child-like Kumaras and are cursed to be born on Earth. Offered seven lives as devotees or three as Vishnu's enemies, they choose three: Hiranyaksha and Hiranyakashipu, Ravana and Kumbhakarna, Shishupala and Dantavakra.
tales.explains: Why Vishnu's great enemies return age after age

tales.title: Daksha Curses Narada
tales.summary: Narada talks Daksha's thousands of sons out of ruling the Earth, twice. Daksha curses him to wander the three worlds forever, then fathers sixty daughters, twenty-seven of whom marry Chandra.
tales.explains: Why Narada never stays in one place; the 27 nakshatras as Chandra's wives

tales.title: The Gods Go Hungry
tales.summary: The gods are starving because Agni cannot carry the yagna offerings to them. Prakriti brings forth the goddess Swaha, who is married to Agni so that offerings reach heaven.

tales.title: Brahma and Vishnu Race
tales.summary: Brahma and Vishnu quarrel over who is greater; a pillar of fire appears. Brahma flies up as a swan and Vishnu digs down as a boar; Brahma lies that he found the top, with a ketaki flower as false witness, and Shiva emerges from the pillar to curse them both.
tales.explains: The linga of fire (Lingodbhava); ketaki barred from Shiva worship; why Brahma has few temples

tales.title: Bala Creates Nine Wonders
tales.summary: The asura Bala defeats Indra, then offers to be the victim at the gods' yagna. His body scatters across the Earth as the nine gems, the navaratnas.

tales.title: Vishnu Gets the Sudarshana Chakra
tales.summary: Vishnu worships Shiva with a thousand lotuses; Shiva hides one, and Vishnu offers his own lotus eye in its place. Shiva gives him the Sudarshana chakra.
tales.note: Another tradition has Vishwakarma forge the chakra from the sun's filings (see tale 14).

tales.title: Sangya Creates Her Twin
tales.summary: Surya's wife Sangya cannot bear his heat, so she makes a shadow double, Chhaya, and leaves. Chhaya favours her own children; Yamuna and Tapti curse each other into rivers, and Yama begins to suspect the truth.
tales.explains: The rivers Yamuna and Tapti; Shani's parentage

tales.title: Dhruva Becomes a Star
tales.summary: Humiliated by his stepmother, the boy Dhruva leaves for the forest and performs fierce austerities. Vishnu grants him a place that never moves: the pole star.

tales.title: Bharat Adopts a Deer
tales.summary: King Bharat gives up his throne for the spiritual life, then rescues an orphaned fawn and grows obsessed with it. Thinking of the deer as he dies, he is reborn as one.

tales.title: Bhrigu Curses Vishnu
tales.summary: While Shukracharya is away the disarmed demons shelter with sage Bhrigu and his wife Kavyamata. The gods attack, Vishnu kills Kavyamata, and Bhrigu curses Vishnu to be born again and again on Earth.

tales.title: Shiva Kills Yama
tales.summary: Markandeya is fated to die at sixteen and clings to a Shiva linga when Yama comes. Shiva slays Yama and revives him only on condition that Markandeya lives forever.
tales.explains: Shiva as Kalantaka; the Mahamrityunjaya mantra

tales.title: Chandra Loses His Light
tales.summary: Chandra favours Rohini over his twenty-six other wives, and their father Daksha curses him to fade away. Shiva softens the curse into waxing and waning, at the place now called Somnath.
tales.explains: The phases of the moon; Somnath; the crescent on Shiva's head

tales.title: Dadhichi Battles the Gods
tales.summary: Sage Dadhichi and King Kshuva argue over whether Brahmins or Kshatriyas are greater; Kshuva kills him with the vajra and Shukracharya revives him. Shiva's blessing makes Dadhichi's bones harder than the vajra, and he outlasts every god sent against him.
tales.explains: Why Dadhichi's bones are unbreakable (set-up for tale 77)

tales.title: Sati Kills Herself
tales.summary: Sati marries Shiva against her father Daksha's will. Humiliated at Daksha's yagna, she gives up her body in its fire, and Shiva's Veerabhadra destroys the rite.
tales.care: Suicide by fire; follow platform self-harm guidance

tales.title: Vishnu Saves the Elephant
tales.summary: Gajendra, king of elephants, is seized by a crocodile and abandoned by his herd. He calls on Vishnu, who kills the crocodile, and Gajendra learns he was once King Indradyumna.

tales.title: Prithu Feeds Mankind
tales.summary: The sages kill the tyrant Vena and draw the good king Prithu from his body. When famine strikes, Prithu chases the Earth, who has taken the form of a cow, and milks her for every kind of food.
tales.explains: Why the Earth is called Prithvi; the start of farming

tales.title: Marisha Takes Ten Husbands
tales.summary: The ten Prachetas meditate for ten thousand years and return to an overgrown, ruined Earth. They start to burn the forests until Chandra stops them and gives them Marisha, daughter of the trees, as their shared wife; their son is Daksha reborn.

tales.title: The Matsya Avatar
tales.summary: Vaivasvata finds a tiny fish that keeps outgrowing every vessel. It is Vishnu, who names him the seventh Manu and has him build a boat to carry life through the coming flood.

tales.title: The Varaha Avatar
tales.summary: Hiranyaksha uses his boon to drag the Earth into the cosmic ocean. Vishnu as the boar Varaha dives in, kills him and lifts the Earth on his tusks.

tales.title: The Narasimha Avatar
tales.summary: Hiranyakashipu's boon seems to rule out every way to die, and he tries again and again to kill his devoted son Prahlad. Vishnu bursts from a pillar as the man-lion and kills him in a gap the boon did not cover.

tales.title: Narasimha Faces Shiva
tales.summary: Narasimha's rage does not subside and threatens the cosmos. Shiva sends Veerabhadra and then intervenes himself to subdue the man-lion and free Vishnu from it.
tales.explains: Shiva as Sharabha (in the Shaiva telling)
tales.care: Shaiva and Vaishnava traditions tell this differently; present it as one tradition's account

tales.title: Indra Attempts Foeticide
tales.summary: Diti vows to bear a son who will kill Indra, and Kashyapa sets her a hundred-year vow of purity. Indra waits for a lapse, enters her womb and cuts the embryo into pieces, which become the Maruts and side with him.

tales.title: Prahlad Is Humbled
tales.summary: King Prahlad asks sage Chyavan for the greatest pilgrimage and is sent to Naimisharanya, where a piece of the Sudarshana chakra fell. In the source tradition he fights the sages Nara and Narayana there and loses. The book's ending was not seen.

tales.title: Taraka Invades Heaven
tales.summary: Diti's son Vajranga defeats Indra but spares him. Vajranga's wife wants a son who will conquer heaven, and Taraka is born; his boon says only a son of Shiva can kill him.

tales.title: Parvati Wins Over Shiva
tales.summary: Kamadeva shoots Shiva with his flower arrow and is burnt to ash by the third eye. Parvati, Sati reborn, wins Shiva through her own austerities instead.

tales.title: Mothers of Kartikeya
tales.summary: Agni interrupts Shiva and Parvati, and Shiva's seed passes from Agni to Ganga to the six Krittikas. The child who forms has six faces and six mothers.
tales.explains: Kartikeya's six heads and his name

tales.title: Kartikeya Battles Taraka
tales.summary: Seven days old, Kartikeya leads the gods against Taraka, sees through his sorcery and kills him with his spear.

tales.title: Shiva Becomes Tripurari
tales.summary: Taraka's three sons are granted three flying fortresses that can be destroyed only when they align. When the moment comes, Shiva burns all three with a single arrow.

tales.title: Andhaka Lusts for Parvati
tales.summary: When Parvati playfully covers Shiva's eyes, a blind child is born from his sweat and raised among the daityas as Andhaka. Granted sight and power, he desires Parvati and is impaled by Shiva.
tales.care: Sexual aggression toward a mother figure

tales.title: Bhringi Challenges Parvati
tales.summary: The sage Bhringi will circle only Shiva, never Parvati. Parvati insists Shiva cannot be worshipped without her; in the common telling she becomes one body with Shiva as Ardhanarishvara and strips Bhringi of what came from the mother until he relents.

tales.title: Churning of the Ocean
tales.summary: Durvasa curses Indra for disrespecting his garland, and heaven loses its fortune. Gods and demons churn the ocean of milk together; Shiva drinks the poison that rises first.
tales.explains: Shiva's blue throat (Neelkantha); the treasures of the ocean

tales.title: Vishnu Becomes Mohini
tales.summary: The demons seize the nectar of immortality. Vishnu as the enchantress Mohini charms them into letting her serve it, and only the gods drink.

tales.title: Kadru and Vinata Place a Bet
tales.summary: Kashyapa's wives Kadru and Vinata bet on the colour of the horse Uchchaishrava's tail. Kadru cheats with the help of her serpent sons, and Vinata becomes her slave until her son Garuda wins her freedom.
tales.explains: The feud between Garuda and the serpents

tales.title: Ganesha Comes to Life
tales.summary: Parvati shapes a boy from turmeric paste and sets him to guard her door. He blocks Shiva, who beheads him, and Parvati's grief forces Shiva to restore him with an elephant's head.

tales.title: Durga Slays Mahishasura
tales.summary: Mahishasura, half buffalo, has a boon that no man can kill him. The gods pool their powers into the goddess Durga, who kills him.

tales.title: Parvati Becomes Gauri
tales.summary: Stung when Shiva jokingly calls her 'Kali', Parvati asks Brahma to make her fair. Her shed dark skin becomes a new goddess, Kaushiki.
tales.care: Skin-colour theme; avoid framing fairness as better

tales.title: Shumbha, Nishumbha and Raktabija
tales.summary: The demon brothers Shumbha and Nishumbha demand the goddess in marriage and send their armies when she refuses. Every drop of Raktabija's blood spawns a new demon, so Kali drinks it before it can fall.

tales.title: Nachiketa Travels to Hell
tales.summary: In anger King Vajashrava gives his son Nachiketa to Yama, and the boy takes him at his word. He goes to the realm of death and wins from Yama the teaching on death and the self.

tales.title: Ganesha and Kartikeya Race
tales.summary: To decide which son marries first, Shiva sets a race around the world. Kartikeya flies off on his peacock; Ganesha walks around his parents and wins.
tales.explains: Why Kartikeya went south (in the traditional telling)

tales.title: Surya Falls from the Sky
tales.summary: The asura king Sukeshi, a devotee of Shiva, teaches his people dharma, and his city in the sky shines so brightly it eclipses the sun. Jealous Surya turns on him, and under Shiva's gaze the sun falls from the sky.
tales.explains: Lolarka in Varanasi (traditional telling; not checked against the book)

tales.title: Bhasmasura Chases Shiva
tales.summary: The demon Vrikasura wins a boon to turn anyone to ash by touching their head, then tries it on Shiva. Vishnu as Mohini draws him into a dance in which he touches his own head.
sources: Bhagavata Purana (as Vrikasura; Vishnu appears as a young student there, the Mohini dance is from later retellings)

tales.title: Chandra Commits Adultery
tales.summary: Chandra elopes with Tara, wife of the gods' guru Brihaspati, and the dispute becomes a war. Tara bears a son, Budh, whose father she must name.
tales.explains: Budh (Mercury) as Chandra's son; start of the lunar dynasty

tales.title: The Vamana Avatar
tales.summary: Bali has taken heaven, and Aditi prays for her sons. Vishnu is born to her as the dwarf Vamana, asks Bali for three steps of land and covers the cosmos in them.

tales.title: Ganga, Lakshmi and Saraswati Fight
tales.summary: Ganga and Saraswati quarrel over Vishnu, and Lakshmi is drawn in as peacemaker. The three curse each other into rivers and a plant on Earth.
tales.explains: Why these goddesses are also rivers (and Lakshmi as tulsi, in the source)

tales.title: Vrinda Curses Vishnu
tales.summary: Fire from Shiva's third eye becomes the demon Jalandhar, who is invincible while his wife Vrinda stays chaste. Vishnu takes Jalandhar's form to deceive her; she curses Vishnu to become stone.

tales.title: Vishnu Is Beheaded
tales.summary: Exhausted from battle, Vishnu sleeps leaning on his strung bow. The gods send termites to gnaw the string, it snaps and his head is cut off; in the source he returns with a horse's head as Hayagriva.

tales.title: Bhrigu Tests the Trinity
tales.summary: The sages ask which god is greatest, and Bhrigu goes to find out. Brahma and Shiva take offence at his rudeness; Vishnu, kicked in the chest, asks if Bhrigu's foot is hurt.
tales.explains: The mark on Vishnu's chest (traditional telling)

tales.title: Sudyumna Becomes a Woman
tales.summary: King Sudyumna rides into an enchanted forest where every man becomes a woman. Shiva lets him alternate between male and female month by month, and as Ila she bears Budh's son.

tales.title: Urvashi Tricks Pururava
tales.summary: Pururava, founder of the lunar dynasty, is cursed by Artha and Kama to lose his wealth and become obsessed with a nymph. The apsara Urvashi lives with him on conditions, and leaves when the gods arrange for them to be broken.

tales.title: Satyavati Is Deceived
tales.summary: Sage Richika wins Princess Satyavati with a thousand white horses and prepares two bowls of charmed rice, one for her and one for her mother. The bowls are swapped, so a Brahmin's line produces a warrior and a king's line a sage.
tales.explains: Why Parashurama is a warrior-Brahmin and Vishwamitra a sage-king

tales.title: Vishwamitra Attacks Vashishtha
tales.summary: King Kaushika covets Vashishtha's wish-granting cow, Kamadhenu, and tries to take her by force. Beaten by the sage's spiritual power, he renounces his throne to become a sage himself: Vishwamitra.

tales.title: Trishanku Falls from the Sky
tales.summary: Exiled prince Satyavrata wants to enter heaven in his body. Vishwamitra sends him up, the gods throw him down, and the sage builds him a heaven of his own where he hangs between the two.

tales.title: Harishchandra Tricks Varuna
tales.summary: Childless King Harishchandra promises Varuna that he will sacrifice the son Varuna gives him, then keeps finding reasons to delay.

tales.title: Harishchandra Is Tested
tales.summary: Possessed by a spirit, Harishchandra insults Vishwamitra and, to atone, gives up his kingdom and everything he owns. Truthful through every loss, he ends up working at a cremation ground.
tales.explains: Harishchandra as the byword for truthfulness

tales.title: Sagara Loses His Sons
tales.summary: Exiled Queen Yadavi survives poison and, helped by sage Aurva, bears Sagara. As king, Sagara's sixty thousand sons hunt for his stolen sacrificial horse and are burnt to ash by the sage Kapila.
tales.explains: The name Sagara; set-up for Ganga's descent

tales.title: Bhagirath Brings Down Ganga
tales.summary: After three generations fail, Bhagirath's austerities bring Ganga down from heaven. Shiva breaks her fall in his hair, and her waters free Sagara's sons.

tales.title: Saraswati Battles Vishnu
tales.summary: Saraswati asks Brahma which goddess is greatest, and he names Lakshmi. She storms back to disrupt his yagna, and Vishnu stands in her way.
tales.explains: Possibly the Kanchi river legend (not checked)

tales.title: The Parashurama Avatar
tales.summary: Jamadagni orders his sons to kill their mother Renuka for a moment's desire. Only Parashurama obeys, then uses his boons to bring her back; he goes on to wipe out the warrior class.

tales.title: Gautama Creates a River
tales.summary: Gautama's hermitage feeds the land through a drought. Jealous hermits trick him into killing a cow, and to wash away the sin he brings the Ganga down as the Godavari.

tales.title: Vishnu Tricks Mura
tales.summary: The danava Mura wins the power to kill with a touch. King Raghu steers him toward challenging Yama, and Vishnu outwits him. The ending was not seen.

tales.title: Narada Gets a New Face
tales.summary: Narada boasts that he has conquered desire, then falls for a princess and asks Vishnu for his beauty; Vishnu gives him a monkey's face. Humiliated, Narada curses Vishnu to lose his wife and need monkeys to win her back.
tales.explains: A Puranic cause for the Ramayana

tales.title: Nimi Loses His Body
tales.summary: King Nimi and sage Vashishtha curse each other out of their bodies over a yagna. Offered his body back, Nimi chooses to live in the eyelids of all beings.
tales.explains: Why we blink (nimesha); the Videha kings

tales.title: Lohajangha and the Saptarishi
tales.summary: The bandit Lohajangha tries to rob the seven sages, who calmly turn his questions back on his life. In the tradition this robber becomes the sage Valmiki.

tales.title: Ravana Seizes Lanka
tales.summary: Kubera is granted the golden city of Lanka. His stepmother Kaikesi pushes her own son Ravana to take it, and he does.

tales.title: The Gods Trick Ravana
tales.summary: Ravana offers his heads to Shiva for a linga to take to Lanka, on condition it never touches the ground. The gods make sure he sets it down on the way.
tales.explains: A Jyotirlinga site (Vaidyanath or Gokarna, depending on telling)

tales.title: Sita Lays Four Curses
tales.summary: Sita performs Dasharath's last rites at the Phalgu river and calls five witnesses. The river, a cow, the fire and a ketaki flower deny it, only a banyan tree tells the truth, and Sita curses the four.
tales.explains: The Phalgu flowing under sand at Gaya; the undying banyan

tales.title: Maya Sita
tales.summary: When Ravana takes Sita, Agni has already hidden the real one; Ravana carries off an illusion. That shadow Sita is later reborn as Draupadi.

tales.title: Rama and the Shudra
tales.summary: A Brahmin blames King Rama for his son's death. The cause is traced to Shambuka, a Shudra practising austerities, whom Rama kills.

tales.title: Agastya Tricks a Mountain
tales.summary: Goaded by Narada, the Vindhya mountain grows until it blocks the sun. Its teacher Agastya asks it to bow so he can pass south, tells it to wait for his return, and never comes back.

tales.title: Dadhichi Offers His Bones
tales.summary: Indra slights his guru Brihaspati, and his replacement Vishvarupa secretly helps the asuras, so Indra kills him. Vishvarupa's father creates Vritra to take revenge, and Dadhichi gives his bones to make the vajra that kills him.

tales.title: Nahusha Becomes Devaraja
tales.summary: With Indra in exile from guilt, the mortal King Nahusha is crowned king of the gods. Pride takes him: he demands Indra's wife and makes sages carry his palanquin until Agastya curses him into a snake.

tales.title: Kacha Steals a Secret
tales.summary: Brihaspati's son Kacha becomes Shukracharya's student to learn the mantra that raises the dead. The asuras kill him repeatedly, and he finally learns it from inside his teacher's stomach, then leaves Devayani behind.

tales.title: Devayani and Sharmishtha
tales.summary: Devayani and the asura princess Sharmishtha fight, and Sharmishtha pushes her into a well. King Yayati pulls Devayani out and marries her; Sharmishtha becomes her servant, then secretly Yayati's lover.

tales.title: Yayati Makes a Demand
tales.summary: Cursed with sudden old age, Yayati asks his five sons to trade him their youth. Only the youngest, Puru, agrees, and he inherits the throne.
tales.explains: Why the Puru (Kuru) line rules and the Yadavas do not

tales.title: Satyatapa Is Tested
tales.summary: When the Himalayan ascetic Satyatapa cuts his finger, sacred ash flows out instead of blood and the finger heals. Curious, Indra sets out to test him. The test itself was not seen.

tales.title: Vishwamitra Accepts Meat
tales.summary: In a terrible drought the starving Vishwamitra decides to cook a dead dog, first as an offering to the gods. The tale asks what dharma means in an emergency.

tales.title: The Birth of Krishna
tales.summary: Devaki and Vasudeva have seen Kansa kill their children in prison. When their eighth child is born, Vasudeva carries him across the Yamuna to safety.

tales.title: Krishna and Yamalarjuna
tales.summary: Yashoda ties the butter-thief to a heavy mortar. Krishna drags it between two trees, uproots them and frees Kubera's sons, whom Narada had cursed.

tales.title: Krishna Tames Kalia
tales.summary: The serpent Kalia poisons the Yamuna. Krishna dives in after a ball, subdues him and sends him away.

tales.title: Krishna Outwits Brahma
tales.summary: Brahma hides Krishna's friends and calves to test him. Krishna becomes every missing boy and calf for a year until Brahma gives in.

tales.title: Krishna Lifts Govardhan
tales.summary: Krishna persuades Vrindavan to honour Mount Govardhan instead of Indra. When Indra sends a storm, Krishna lifts the mountain to shelter everyone.

tales.title: Krishna Heals Kubja
tales.summary: On the way to Kansa's wrestling match in Mathura, Krishna calls a shunned hunchbacked maid beautiful and straightens her body.

tales.title: Pradyumna and the Maid
tales.summary: Krishna and Rukmini's firstborn, Pradyumna, arrives as the Yadavas settle in Dwaravati. In the source he is stolen as an infant by the demon Shambara and raised by a maid who is Rati, Kama's wife, reborn.
tales.explains: Kama reborn as Pradyumna (links to tale 32)

tales.title: The Theft of Shyamantaka
tales.summary: Surya gives Satrajit the jewel Shyamantaka, which produces gold every day. When it goes missing Krishna is accused, so he tracks it down to clear his name.

tales.title: Krishna and Sudama
tales.summary: The poor Brahmin Sudama visits his childhood friend Krishna but is too proud to ask for help. He leaves with nothing and comes home to find his family rich.

tales.title: Krishna and Narakasura
tales.summary: The Earth's son Narakasura conquers heaven and steals Aditi's earrings. Krishna kills him.

tales.title: The Battle for Parijat
tales.summary: In Indra's garden Satyabhama falls for the heavenly parijat tree. Krishna uproots it for her and fights Indra to keep it.

tales.title: The False Vishnu
tales.summary: King Paundraka decides he is the true Vasudeva, dresses up with fake divine emblems and challenges Krishna, who kills him.

tales.title: Arjuna Is Humbled
tales.summary: Arjuna vows to save a Brahmin's newborn after seven have vanished at birth, and seals the house with arrows; the baby still disappears. Krishna takes him beyond the universe to find the lost children.

tales.title: Veda and Bhila
tales.summary: Veda, a devout priest, finds raw meat left in his Shiva shrine every day. He watches and sees Shiva bless Bhila, the hunter leaving it, over his own ritual worship.

tales.title: Krishna Battles Shiva
tales.summary: Banasura's daughter Usha dreams of her destined husband, Krishna's grandson Aniruddha, and he is brought to her secretly. Bana imprisons him, and Krishna fights Shiva, Bana's protector, to free him.

tales.title: End of the Yadu Clan
tales.summary: Gandhari's curse and a sage's curse, provoked by Samba's prank, come due. The drunken Yadavas kill each other at Prabhasa, and Krishna waits for death under a tree.

tales.title: Janmejaya's Snake Sacrifice
tales.summary: The serpent Takshak kills King Parikshit, and his son Janmejaya starts a sacrifice that drags every snake into the fire.
